subject.title: [Feature]: 内置健壮性机制：Watchdog、全局错误处理、自动恢复

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in Gateway watchdog/recovery ladder, and which recovery actions should be default, opt-in, or out of scope?
rationale: The request crosses process supervision, config/schema, doctor repair, notifications, degraded startup, and security-sensitive operator authority, so source inspection cannot safely choose permanent product semantics.

options.title: Keep umbrella and design opt-in recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

options.title: Split into canonical narrower issues
options.body: Replace this broad umbrella with separate issues for process watchdog, health schema, error policy, degraded startup, and notifications.

options.title: Reject core ownership
options.body: Close the request as out of core scope and document supervisor, plugin, or operator-owned recovery patterns instead.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and design opt-in recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main crash-loop breaker and adjacent fatal-error/gateway lifecycle history make this the best available owner for the product boundary decision.
